keyFindings.description: [overflow-anchor:none] takes the browser's place-keeping away for every height change above a scrolled-back reader, and the hook replaces it only on the rebuild path: the ResizeObserver returns unless the viewport is following (use-live-follow.ts:301-310). Pictures are the concrete source - MarkdownBody renders DispatchPicture for a body's images and the img is loading="lazy" with no reserved box (DispatchPicture.tsx:22, :81-87) - so after a rebuild, whose settle compensates in the commit the turns land in while the re-created pictures above are still 0px, each one that loads pushes the reader further down. Not blocking: the approved spec v9 says in terms that content landing above the reader still shifts the text under them and that this issue does not change that, so compensating every above-growth is new behaviour beyond the approved scope. Recorded on the PR body's Not proven / risk line and sent to the architect as a follow-up candidate (give the ResizeObserver the non-following case, restoring the remembered turn as settleRebuild already does).

A turn's key flips under a scrolled-back reader when the stored copy of a taken-over message lands: the turn renders first under its streamed frame id and is re-keyed to dispatch:<id> once the stored list refetches (:88-99, turnKey at dispatch-marks.ts:48-53). seen is a snapshot taken in follow() (use-live-follow.ts:151-160), so a turn the reader had already seen reappears as unseen and the control reads "Jump to latest · 1 new" for a turn on screen; if their remembered turn is the re-keyed one and they do not scroll again, settleRebuild's turn === undefined branch sends them to the live end on the next rebuild although their turn survived. Narrow (the refetch lands within a moment of the frame, and remembered is re-read on every scroll) and cosmetic in its common form.

The rebuild watcher's lifetime is a passive effect while its arming is a layout effect, handed across through pendingRebuild/armedIds/rebuildWatcher. In a commit where viewport changes identity and the rebuild branch is reached, the layout effect arms the old watcher object (passive cleanup has not run), the cleanup then disconnects it and the replacement watcher is never armed, so pendingRebuild stays true and that rebuild never settles. Very narrow: it needs a viewport replacement (an ErrorBoundary reset) in the same commit as a rebuild whose turns lag their ids, and the tester reports no stream input reaches that boundary today.
lastScrollHeight is written on every record (:147) and read nowhere in the package - residue of the deleted settle fingerprint. Dead state on the hot path.

rememberTurn is a near-verbatim second copy of features/shell/ViewportAnchor.tsx's rowAtCenter, its two probe constants included (PROBE_STEPS 5, PROBE_STEP_PX 8 against probeSteps 5, probeStepPx 8 at ViewportAnchor.tsx:35-36). Round 1's O(turns) scan went, but by duplication rather than by one shared hit-test helper. Related: END_TOLERANCE_PX does double duty as the probe inset at :68,:70, and the fallback to the first turn when every probe misses restores an absolute distance from the top of the transcript, which is the behaviour the feature exists to avoid after a budgeted rebuild.

verifiedMyself: Round 1's two blocking defects are fixed and the fixes are pinned, mutation-measured by me at this head: removing settleRebuild's compensation fails `a rebuild that still holds the remembered turn keeps it where the reader had it` and `a rebuild whose turns reach the DOM a commit later still holds the remembered turn` (Expected 50, Received 150); neutralising the element-keyed re-baseline layout effect fails `a replaced viewport element still answers the reader's scroll` (Expected 300, Received 0); dropping `viewport` from the scroll listener's deps, which is round 1's binding, fails five rows. Baseline: bun test web/src/features/agent-view, 52 pass 0 fail.

The spec's eleventh proof line now has its browser row, agent-view.e2e.ts:1252, driving the production deferred path through ?as=drop: a rebuild that drops eight turns and adds two, the newest turn above the composer with no control, the next published turn followed, then a scroll back asserted at threadScrollTop 1000 - which is also the browser half of round 1's first defect.

All six threads I opened carry the implementer's answer and are resolved by it as the pull request's author; there are no bot threads. CI read on GitHub: required set lint, typecheck, test, pr-title (main's rulesets; branch protection carries none), all completed/success at the code head c16a82b7c5da, beside dispatch, dispatch-memory, envoy-go, envoy-go-race, envoy-e2e-local, envoy-smoke, envoy-infra-go, pi-legion and build; compare c16a82b7...5db35f1d lists only the two .legion/ handoffs.

The ?as=drop hook's gate re-read at this head: mounted only under TestHooksEnabled (routes_table.go:184-190, authHuman), requireHuman at agent_stream.go:236, 503 STREAM_UNAVAILABLE unless the relay is the in-memory source, one validated session UUID's viewers. The nil-Frame reservation is now on the Frame contract (agentstream.go:21-25) and the NATS source cannot produce one (make(Frame, len) is non-nil).
architectQuestion: The architect asked whether [overflow-anchor:none] must be pinned by a test before merge. My answer, recorded here as it asked: no, and I approve without it. The tester measured that removing the class leaves the whole agent-view browser suite green, so the only available lock is an assertion that the computed overflow-anchor is none - a test of the source text rather than of a behaviour, which is the shape this repository's norms refuse. What is load-bearing is the hook's own compensation, and that is now pinned twice over: the browser rebuild row fails when it is deleted (the tester measured it, and I mutation-measured the two unit rows myself), where at round 1 the same mutation passed. The hazard itself is named at the site, AgentThread.tsx:400-404. The gap I would rather see closed is that packages/dispatch/AGENTS.md's scrolling paragraph, rewritten in this round, does not mention the class at all - a documentation line, not a round.
thermo: thermonuclear-deep-review and thermonuclear-code-quality both run once at 5db35f1d63313924b891f04e9e7d7254f4e253fa. Deep review: one Medium (the above-growth compensation gap), one Low (the turn-key flip), one Minor (dead lastScrollHeight), with the rewritten observe, the element-keyed re-binding, the elementFromPoint probe, the Go hook and round-1 regression checks all clean. Code quality: round 1's majors 1, 2 and 3 settled, 4 (replayCount plumbing) unanswered, and new findings on the second layout effect, the watcher's cross-effect wiring, the duplicated hit test and the e2e file's size. Every finding I carried I verified against the code myself; none of them stands as a correctness defect at this head.
